edit.description: `refuse_ungoverned` (line 1119) builds `member: host_address(kind, member)` — a host-less `<kind>:<name>` — while both callers hold the host: `nested_file_path` (line 1240) is the nested-file-child branch, and `member_projection_path` (line 1357) carries a `host: Option<&str>` of its own. Thread that column in and spell `member_address_under(host, kind, member)` (line 2450), the one home `ae1c41e7` routed five finding sites through. Same fix for `nested_file_path`'s `refuse` closure (line 1206, `member: name.to_string()`), whose `host` is its own parameter — so the no-host arm still reads `kind:name` and the first arm (no host at all) is unchanged. Re-word both variants' `member` field docs off "The member's `kind:name` address" (`UngovernedProjection` line 538, `NestedFileLocus` under line 494).

The regression, beside `mod host_qualified_addresses` (line 902) and the whole-address assertions at line 1920: a nested member whose host kind templates no file layer refuses with `NestedFileLocus` naming `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>`, and two same-keyed children under two distinct hosts refuse distinguishably (one emit per fixture — the refusal aborts the pass, so the two addresses cannot both appear in one report). Add the `UngovernedProjection` case if an admissible declaration reaches that branch (a directory-unit child kind under a host pattern carrying a directory prefix places `<name>/<entry>`, which the pattern cannot find); if no admissible declaration does, say so in the commit body rather than contriving one.

summary: The two placement refusals name a nested file child by its whole address — UngovernedProjection and NestedFileLocus still spell a host-less kind:name

tests.asserts: a nested file child's `NestedFileLocus` refusal names `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>`, never the bare key; two hosts' same-keyed children are refused under two addresses a reader can tell apart; a top-level member's refusal still reads `kind:name`
